comment: Authoritative sources only. The organising principle: never monitor an individual municipality's own website. Monitor the state-level register that the municipality is legally required to report into. Ohio's ~600 municipalities collapse to one Department of Taxation file; Pennsylvania's ~2,500 Act 32 jurisdictions collapse to one DCED register. That is what turns '7,400 jurisdictions' into roughly 60 things to watch.

sources.title: PA DCED Municipal Statistics — Act 32 EIT rates and PSD codes
sources.expectedChange: rolling; most changes effective 1 Jan
sources.note: DCED is the only legally recognised source for PSD codes and EIT rates. Individual tax collection bureaus republish it and are NOT authoritative. KNOWN GAP, found by auditing what was actually captured rather than trusting the fetch succeeded: this URL returns the Municipal Statistics SEARCH FORM, not the register behind it. The captured page is an ASP.NET form — __VIEWSTATE, a Search control, and ZERO rate figures anywhere in 29KB. It fetches 200 and hashes stable, so the monitor reports it healthy every day while telling us nothing: a form does not change when the ~2,500 PSD/EIT rates behind it do. This is the largest local-tax dataset in the project and it is effectively UNWATCHED. Tried and failed to reach the real register: munstats.pa.gov/Reports/ReportInformation2.aspx with report=eitPitLstReg_Dyn and =EitPitLstRegisterPrintable, and a RealTimeRegister query on the form URL, all returned network errors. dced.pa.gov's PSD-codes-and-EIT-rates page DOES load (148KB) but is chiefly a landing page — only a handful of rate-like figures — so it was not adopted as a substitute that would look like a fix without being one. What is needed: the 'EIT / PIT / LST Tax Registers (Real-Time) — Printable' export, whose stable URL was not found this pass. Until then, treat PA local rates as verified only as of their data file's own verifiedOn date, NOT as monitored.

urlHistory.reason: Domain munstats.pa.gov stopped resolving entirely (DNS NXDOMAIN, confirmed by nslookup and a curl exit-6). PA moved Municipal Statistics under apps.dced.pa.gov. Found by the harvester sweep on its first real run — exactly the source-rot this monitoring exists to catch, and a reminder that a registered URL is itself a thing that decays.

sources.title: Texas — UI taxable wage base (via US DOL Significant Measures of State UI Tax Systems)
sources.expectedChange: annual; unemployment wage base and employer rate schedule are set each autumn
sources.note: REPOINTED after twc.texas.gov proved unfetchable by any machine: every path tried returns an HTTP 202 WAF challenge instead of the page — the rates page, the no-www variant, an alternate rates path, the news index, and even a PDF under /sites/default/files. The block is domain-wide, not path-specific. Three other routes were tried and rejected: statutes.capitol.texas.gov is an Angular SPA that serves only a shell to a plain fetch (same failure class as the Municode wall already documented for Birmingham); law.justia.com 403s; data.texas.gov fetches but carries no wage-base figure. This DOL report is the one authoritative, fetchable source that does: verified it contains the row 'TEXAS ... Fixed 9,000 ... Taxable Wage Base ($)', independently corroborating the 9000 in data/states/TX-2026.json. TWO HONEST LIMITS. (1) It LAGS: DOL publishes annually and the 2024 edition is still the newest as of 2026-08 (the 25 and 26 filenames both 404), so a wage-base change would surface here late rather than promptly — a late signal being strictly better than the none we had. (2) It covers the UI wage base only, not income-tax withholding — which costs nothing HERE, because Texas levies no income tax and the wage base is the only figure in its data file that can move, and DOL's own report calls it 'Fixed'. Do NOT copy this URL to a state that has an income tax; for those, the state's own withholding guide remains the source. The same report does cross-check every state's wage base, so it is worth reading directly when auditing suiEmployer figures.
